## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Discovery[Component Discovery]
        A[Model Registry Scanner]
        B[Tool Catalog Monitor]
        C[Runtime Version Tracker]
        D[Prompt Template Index]
    end
    subgraph Assembly[Stack Assembly]
        E[Compatibility Checker]
        F[Stack Composer]
    end
    subgraph Evaluation[Benchmark Evaluation]
        G[Accuracy Evaluator]
        H[Latency Profiler]
        I[Token Cost Analyzer]
        J[Multi-Objective Scorer]
    end
    subgraph Governance[Policy and Provenance]
        K[Policy Engine]
        L[Provenance Ledger]
        M[Rollback Controller]
    end
    subgraph Runtime[Production Runtime]
        N[Active Stack]
        O[Shadow Stack]
    end
    A --> E
    B --> E
    C --> E
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> O
    O --> G
    O --> H
    O --> I
    G --> J
    H --> J
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K -->|Promote| N
    K -->|Reject| L
    K -->|Regress| M
    M --> N
    F --> L
    K --> L
```

## Sequence Diagram

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Disc as Discovery Engine
    participant Compat as Compatibility Checker
    participant Comp as Stack Composer
    participant Bench as Benchmark Runner
    participant Score as Multi-Objective Scorer
    participant Policy as Policy Engine
    participant Prov as Provenance Ledger
    participant Prod as Production Runtime

    loop Continuous Optimization Cycle
        Disc->>Compat: New components detected
        Compat->>Comp: Compatible component sets
        Comp->>Bench: Candidate stack assembled
        Bench->>Score: Accuracy, latency, cost results
        Score->>Policy: Ranked stack configurations
        alt Superior configuration found
            Policy->>Prov: Record decision rationale
            Policy->>Prod: Promote new stack
        else Regression detected
            Policy->>Prov: Log rejection reason
            Policy->>Prod: Rollback to prior stack
        end
    end
```

## State Diagram

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Scanning
    Scanning --> ComponentFound: New version detected
    ComponentFound --> CompatCheck: Validate dependencies
    CompatCheck --> Assembling: Compatible
    CompatCheck --> Scanning: Incompatible
    Assembling --> Benchmarking: Candidate stack ready
    Benchmarking --> Scoring: Results collected
    Scoring --> Promoting: Exceeds current stack
    Scoring --> Rejected: Below threshold
    Promoting --> Active: Policy approved
    Promoting --> RollingBack: Regression in production
    RollingBack --> Active: Prior stack restored
    Rejected --> Scanning: Log and continue
    Active --> Scanning: Next cycle
```

## Component Evaluation Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Inputs[Stack Components]
        M[Models]
        P[Prompts]
        T[Tools]
        R[Runtimes]
    end
    subgraph Combine[Combinatorial Assembly]
        CC[Candidate Stacks]
    end
    subgraph Evaluate[Org-Specific Benchmarks]
        E1[Task Accuracy]
        E2[Response Latency]
        E3[Token Usage]
        E4[Dollar Cost]
    end
    subgraph Decide[Decision Layer]
        PO[Pareto Optimization]
        PE[Policy Constraints]
    end
    subgraph Output[Outcome]
        PR[Promoted Config]
        PL[Provenance Record]
    end
    M --> CC
    P --> CC
    T --> CC
    R --> CC
    CC --> E1
    CC --> E2
    CC --> E3
    CC --> E4
    E1 --> PO
    E2 --> PO
    E3 --> PO
    E4 --> PO
    PO --> PE
    PE --> PR
    PE --> PL
```

INVENTION: --- invention-id: invention-20260716-153029 company: RedHat created: 2026-07-16T15:30:42 --- # Invention Idea We propose an autonomous optimization engine that continuously discovers, evaluates, and evolves the complete software stack underpinning an AI agent rather than treating models, prompts, tools, and runtimes as static infrastructure. The system periodically identifies newly available components, automatically assembles compatible execution stacks, evaluates them against organization-specific benchmarks, and compares their performance across multiple objectives such as accuracy, latency, token consumption, and cost. Based on these evaluations, a policy engine promotes superior configurations while maintaining complete provenance explaining every architectural decision and enabling rapid rollback if regressions occur. This creates a self-improving agent platform capable of continuously adapting to the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem without requiring manual engineering intervention.
